scope: Three fresh-noise seeds on one fixed source latent; qualitative comparison, no success-rate estimate.
fixed_intervention: Same step40 cat latent, same re-noising coefficients to sigma4, same dog prompt and46-step UniPC restart.
semantic_result: All three show recognizable golden-retriever-like dogs throughout the inspected81-frame sequences, with no visible return to cat identity.
common_behavior: All remain broadly in rear/side or rear-three-quarter views, heading left/away rather than following the requested left-to-right full-side-view path. This resembles the original source orientation; this comparison alone does not isolate the causal source of that resemblance.

samples.observations: Orange-brown coat, raised-leg gait, lower/bunched tail, patchier grass with pale bare streaks. Rear-side view becomes more rear-facing. Fur and limb contours are somewhat smeared.
Longer-looking body and more side-on initial view; low sweeping feathered tail. Turns to rear-three-quarter and recedes markedly across the grass. Some waxy fur and awkward limb contours.
Rounder torso, upright pale fluffy tail, rear-three-quarter view from the start. More conspicuous rounded underside and rubbery hindquarter/leg shapes.

conclusion: Fresh noise changes visible dog appearance, body/tail pose, gait and background texture while all three retain dog identity. These are three diverse semantic conversions, not anatomically flawless outputs.
review_evidence: All81 frames per result in chronological sheets, full-resolution frames0/40/80, and matched six-frame contact sheet.
